messages:
jacob_cust: Hey team — we just found what looks like a Redwood API key embedded inside a Sentry crash dump that we uploaded yesterday. Legal is breathing down our neck for retention/audit details. Do we need to rotate immediately? What exact logs/audit exports do you need from us to triage?

maya_support: sorry to hear that — yes rotate immediately as a precaution. Can you confirm: (1) the exact API key id (prefix like rk_...), (2) any request IDs or timestamps around suspicious activity, and (3) whether the key is still active in the console?

jacob_cust: key looks like rk_live_4f3a... I don't see any obvious spikes but we can't be sure. Sentry file name is crash-2026-03-15-13.zip. We don't have request IDs. Legal asked for audit logs for the last 7 days and proof of rotation.

liam_security: immediate checklist from security: 
- Revoke the compromised key (create new key first if you need zero-downtime).
- Export audit logs for the key: calls, ips, x-request-id if present, and timestamp range.
- Check for any tokens or refresh flows that might have leaked the key to third parties.
- If customer data might be involved, preserve the Sentry artifact and hash it for chain-of-custody.

maya_support: steps we can do from support side once you confirm revocation: 
1) We can flag the key id and freeze it to stop all traffic (fast).
2) Pull last-7-day audit events for that key and send a redacted dump to your legal contact.
3) If you need an incident packet (IP list, geos, sample request headers) we can assemble it and route to security + legal.

jordan_eng: practical rotation steps (minimal downtime):
- Create a new API key in the console (or via API).
- Roll new key to a small subset of clients (canary) for 10-15 minutes.
- Revoke old key after verifying success.

Example curl to create/revoke (replace placeholders):
```
# create new key via console recommended; programmatic revoke example
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/keys/revoke \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ADMIN_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{"key_id":"rk_live_4f3a..."}'
```

maya_support: note — if your key material is wrapped by a customer-managed KMS/HSM, rotation steps differ. If the service account used to sign requests relies on a customer KMS key, you'll need to rotate that key and update the key reference in our console. Tell us if you use KMS (AWS KMS / GCP KMS / Azure KeyVault) or an HSM so we can include provider-specific commands.

jacob_cust: we use AWS KMS for signing, yes. We also have a small fleet of embedded mobile agents that update weekly.

liam_security: for AWS KMS: rotate the CMK and update the key ARN in your app config. Also: enable key usage logs (CloudTrail) and export CloudTrail events for the timeframe. On our side we will correlate any calls that used that API key to IPs and provide an events CSV.

maya_support: to pull audit logs from our platform we'll need the key_id, your account id, and desired timeframe. If you want the raw events we can generate a signed S3 export (7 day retention by default for export bundles). Do you want us to proceed with that?

jacob_cust: yes please, proceed. Also legal needs a statement of retention policy and a signed export — can you include the hash and timestamp?

audit_bot: Redwood Audit exports: default platform audit retention is 90 days. We can generate an export bundle with SHA256 manifest and delivery to a customer S3 bucket or secure link.

maya_support: confirmed — we'll open an escalation ticket to security & legal. Next steps for you: rotate keys now (create new key + canary), tell us the new key id when ready, and we will freeze the old key and produce the export with manifest. We'll also include a short incident summary suitable for legal.

jordan_eng: quick repro step for us to validate: if you can find one suspicious request and share the x-request-id (or full request headers redacting user PII) we can trace the backend logs and show exact handler and model used. If none, we'll default to key-level event export.

jacob_cust: thanks — creating new key now and will share when done. Please open ticket and cc my legal contact emma.

maya_support: on it — escalation ticket opened (#INC-2026-4597). cc @liam_security @jordan_eng. We'll post the export link here when ready. :lock: 

liam_security: one more recommendation: rotate any secondary secrets that may have been derived from the same build artifact (client config files). Also rotate any Sentry DSN keys if they were shared alongside.

jacob_cust: noted. appreciate the fast help.

maya_support: keep us posted — we'll attach the export + signed manifest to the ticket and notify you when the freeze is complete.
